questions.q: Why does doing nothing feel like a waste of time today?
a: The line between work and leisure has blurred
People have more free time than ever
Rest has become too expensive to afford
Modern jobs require less mental effort
questions.why: Lesson one says job insecurity and the information age condition people to believe they should never stop working.

questions.q: What is attention-holding architecture, as Odell describes it?
a: Art or spaces that direct attention to the present
Buildings designed to hold large crowds
Apps built to keep users scrolling
Museums that display famous paintings
questions.why: Lesson two defines it as anything that encourages being present, such as a performance built around watching a sunset.

questions.q: What does Scott Polach's Applause Encouraged ask people to do?
a: Sit quietly and simply notice the sunset
Applaud loudly as the sun goes down
Photograph the sunset from every angle
Discuss the artwork with a guide
questions.why: The summary describes guests sitting in folding chairs, watching the sunset without pictures, then clapping.

questions.q: How does the author handle rude drivers?
a: She assumes they may be having a hard day
She honks until they move aside
She speeds up to pass them
She reports them to the police
questions.why: Lesson three says she lets it go because she cannot know what the other person is going through.

questions.q: What choice does the book draw from David Foster's speech about frustration?
a: See others as obstacles or as people with their own burdens
Respond with anger or with complete silence
Avoid crowds or learn to enjoy them
Work harder or accept a smaller life
questions.why: Lesson three says you can focus on your own hunger and pain, or pause to remember that others have complicated lives too.
